stories.title: LIVE UPDATES: Army detonating nation's stockpile of lead azide in Iowa
stories.summary: After several delays, the U.S. Army is detonating a stockpile of lead azide that officials say is unsafe to move due to the risk of spontaneous explosion.

stories.title: Latest maps provided by US Army show potential locations of lead exposure during Wednesday's controlled detonation
stories.summary: The maps outline the potential for where lead may be present in the air and where lead may be deposited on the ground.

stories.title: IAAAP holds press conference on Army detonation
stories.summary: A joint press conference was held today to provide an update on the plan for the controlled detonation of the lead-azide supply.

stories.title: Middletown lead azide detonation scheduled for 9 a.m. Wednesday, emergency alert says
stories.summary: Residents received an emergency alert Tuesday morning warning of possible evacuations and advising people within 20 miles of the plant to take precautions.

stories.title: 'The danger is immediate' | Gov. Reynolds shares statement of support in lead azide detonation
stories.summary: The U.S. Army is expected to detonate 68 barrels, or nearly five tons, of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown Wednesday morning.

stories.title: Southeast Iowa livestock farmers testing for lead ahead of Middletown detonation
stories.summary: An animal feed delivery company is handing out lead test strips to its customers to get a baseline reading on water used for animals.

stories.title: Iowa Poison Control Center shares guidance ahead of lead detonation
stories.summary: The IPCC worked with the Iowa HHS, Iowa Homeland Security and Emergency Management and other state partners to develop the tips.

stories.title: Army to move forward with lead azide detonation in Iowa on Wednesday following court ruling
stories.summary: Acting Army Sec. Adam Telle said the detonation will take place at some point on Wednesday morning.

stories.title: US Army to detonate lead azide Wednesday. What Iowa leaders are saying
stories.summary: Army officials said the material has become increasingly unstable and poses a growing risk if left in storage.

stories.title: Trump says he ordered Army not to detonate lead azide in Iowa without court approval, stay now lifted
stories.summary: Monday's post on Truth Social is the first time the president himself has spoken out on the Army's planned detonation of nearly five tons of lead azide.

stories.title: Winter weather raises risk from unstable lead azide stockpile, expert says
stories.summary: A chemistry professor says freezing conditions could increase the risk of an uncontrolled explosion, adding urgency to the Army's planned detonation.

stories.title: What is lead azide? Army plans controlled detonation of hazardous explosives in Iowa
stories.summary: The Army plans to destroy 5 tons of unstable lead azide explosives at an Iowa ammunition plant, despite legal attempts to stop the detonation.
